guarantees.claim: When mux_err.valid is high, error_o is assigned the entire mux_err struct regardless of fsm_err.valid.
When mux_err.valid is low and fsm_err.valid is high, error_o is assigned the fsm_err struct.
For all other combinations of fsm_err.valid and mux_err.valid, error_o is driven to a zeroed error structure (valid=0, code=ErrNone, info=0).
guarantees.cond: default branch when no other case matched

assumptions.claim: fsm_err and mux_err are structs of the same type as error_o, with fields valid, code, info, and ErrNone is a defined enumeration value.
assumptions.risk: Type mismatch would cause compilation error or incorrect width extension/truncation; undefined ErrNone would cause compile failure.

uncertain_points.claim: If either valid signal is X or Z, the casez may not match the expected branch. For example, if fsm_err.valid = 1 and mux_err.valid = X, the default branch is taken, outputting a no-error value and suppressing the real fsm_err.
uncertain_points.risk: Real error from FSM could be masked during simulation or when valid signals are uninitialized/metastable, leading to missed error reporting.
